What the maker says (9)
  • Good forPETG HF maintains the inherent strengths of regular PETG, providing superior resistance to water, UV, and temperatures. Tougher and more durable than PLA, with higher temperature resistance, it's the perfect choice for printing outdoor items such as planter pots, bird cages, watering cans, and automotive parts. Additionally, it's ideal for outdoor toys that require long-term exposure and the ability to withstand impacts, collisions, and falls.Bambu Lab, PETG HF official maker product pagep. 1: exact product features/description/application tips, source text line 138
  • BenefitsBambu PETG HF is a fully optimized PETG filament designed specifically for high-speed printing.Bambu Lab, Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet - PETG HFp. 1
  • BenefitsWith a default printing speed that is twice as fast as standard PETG filaments, PETG HF takes your printing efficiency to new heights.Bambu Lab, Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet - PETG HFp. 1
  • BenefitsOffering greater durability and toughness than PLA, PETG HF is the ideal choice for creating long-lasting items with an improved finish and faster production times.Bambu Lab, Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet - PETG HFp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsIt's not recommended to anneal prints of PETG HF, because only very limited promotion of properties can obtain while prints with not very simple shape and structure may deform obviously.Bambu Lab, Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet - PETG HFp. 3
  • Pitfalls and limitationsPETG HF is discontinued and will not be restocked once sold out. A new and improved PETG is available now! Buy Now >Bambu Lab, PETG HF official maker product pagep. 1: exact product features/description/application tips, source text line 49
  • Surface finishThe new matte finish not only enhances the aesthetic by smoothing out uneven gloss during speed transitions but also provides a consistently uniform look.Bambu Lab, Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet - PETG HFp. 1
  • Odour and emissionsOdor OdorlessBambu Lab, Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet - PETG HFp. 3
  • Supports and removalSupport Material Support for PETGBambu Lab, Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet - PETG HFp. 2

What the maker says (6)
  • Good forOptimized for exceptional light transmittance, Bambu PETG Translucent provides unmatched levels of translucency. * Please note that the transparency of the prints may vary depending on factors such as size and structure, as well as printing parameters (including speed, nozzle temperature, and infill density).Bambu Lab, PETG Translucent official maker product pagep. 1: exact product features/description/application tips, source text line 135
  • BenefitsThis specially tuned filament minimizes common issues like nozzle sticking, leakage, and clumping during the printing process, providing a hassle-free experience compared to ordinary PETG materials.Bambu Lab, Technical Data Sheet V1.0 PETG Translucentp. 1
  • BenefitsThe filament also exhibits water resistance, UV resistance, and resistance to temperature changes, making it an excellent choice for outdoor applications.Bambu Lab, Technical Data Sheet V1.0 PETG Translucentp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsIt's not recommended to anneal prints of PETG Translucent, because only very limited promotion of properties can obtain while prints with not very simple shape and structure may deform obviously.Bambu Lab, Technical Data Sheet V1.0 PETG Translucentp. 3
  • Odour and emissionsOdor OdorlessBambu Lab, Technical Data Sheet V1.0 PETG Translucentp. 3
  • Printing advicePrinting PETG Translucent with the appropriate print parameters can achieve an appearance ranging from tinted translucent to tinted transparent. Learn more about Printing tips for transparent PETG on WIKI.Bambu Lab, PETG Translucent official maker product pagep. 1: exact product features/description/application tips, source text line 157

(QIDI, Technical Data Sheet QIDI ToughPETG-HF, p. 1). The maker's statement, not a test result.

  • BenefitsQIDI ToughPETG-HF is a toughness modified PETG developed specifically for FDM, which provides excellent high speed printability by improving material flow and have better mechanical strength and heat resistance compared to PLA.QIDI, Technical Data Sheet QIDI ToughPETG-HFp. 1

What the maker says (14)
  • Good forOur low-gloss PETG is perfect for applications that require the performance of PETG, but a more sophisticated fit and finish.3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1
  • BenefitsSuperior Chemical Resistance vs. ABS3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1
  • Warping and shrinkageAmorphous: Low shrink and warp3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1
  • Surface finish3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG is a specialty grade of PETG that offers a low-gloss, high-tech look.3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1
  • Surface finishThe low-gloss helps hide the layer lines and offers a more “technical look” to the parts as compared to higher gloss filaments.3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1
  • Surface finishLow-gloss sheen – excellent finish3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1
  • Adhesion between layersIdeal extruder temp is 260 to 280°C, or higher depending on your printer / thermocouple set-up – some users report requiring temps up to 290°C to obtain optimal layer bonding.3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1
  • Adhesion between layersThe low-gloss additive in this material requires a higher extruder temp to achieve good layer bonding than you usually use for standard PETG.3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1
  • Adhesion between layersYou may need to increase nozzle temps by 20°C or higher than standard PETG settings if you have layer bonding issues.3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1
  • Moisture sensitivityLow moisture absorption: 3X lower vs. ABS3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1
  • Odour and emissionsVery low odor emitted during printing3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1
  • Supports and removalOur Aquatek X1 water soluble support works great to create complex parts.3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1
  • Printing adviceLow Gloss PETG does NOT printer the same as standard PETG.3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1
  • Printing adviceMagigoo Bed Prep Adhesive , or Clean glass w/ 4mm Kapton Tape3DXTECH, 3DXPro™ Low-Gloss PETG Filamentp. 1

What the maker says (49)
  • Good forIt is an excellent choice for printing mechanically stressed parts.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Good forThanks to strength and durability, PETG is a great choice for mechanical parts.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Good forAlso plastic parts on Original Prusa i3 MK3 are made of PETG material.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Good forPETG is perfect for printing any holders or clamps in your workroom.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Good forBecause of the very good layer adhesion, the PETG prints are suitable for waterproof applications.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Good forIts use is universal but especially suitable for mechanical parts and both indoor and outdoor use.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • BenefitsCompared to PLA, it is more heat resistant, more flexible and less brittle.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • BenefitsHigh temperature resistancePrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • BenefitsEasy to printPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • BenefitsStrength and DurabilityPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • BenefitsSimple to sandPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • BenefitsPETG is a very tough material with good thermal resistance.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • BenefitsIt’s almost as easy to print as PLA, but it can offer many mechanical properties that PLA prints just cannot achieve.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • BenefitsGlycol modifies the properties of PET, so that it’s easier to print, less brittle and clearer when printing with semi-transparent variants.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • BenefitsPETG is ductilePrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • BenefitsIt has a healthy amount of flex which can prevent parts from breaking under pressure.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • BenefitsIf you can handle the oozing and strong adhesion, you’ll be left with a very durable print, that is considerably temperature resistant and usable for both indoor and outdoor use.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsStrong adhesion to the bed - be careful when you’re removing the printPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsNot suitable for tiny partsPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsPossibility of stringingPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsPoor bridging characteristicsPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsCannot be acetone smoothed like ABSPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsProne to scratches (more than PLA)Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsUnlike PLA or ABS, PETG tends to ooze a bit and may leave strings of plastic on your print.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Warping and shrinkageLow shrinking and warpingPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Warping and shrinkagePETG has almost no warping , so printing large objects isn’t a problem.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Warping and shrinkagePETG has a low thermal expansion, so even when printing big objects, and without an enclosure, it rarely lifts from the bed and warps.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Surface finishGlossy and smooth surface finishPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Adhesion between layersStrong layer to layer adhesionPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Adhesion between layersBecause of the very good layer adhesionPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Adhesion between layersThe higher filament temperature will aid extra strong layer adhesion.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Moisture sensitivityLow water absorptionPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Odour and emissionsMostly odorless while printingPrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Supports and removalSupports are harder to removePrusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceYou can fight this with increasing retraction and playing with hotend temperature, but if you use our filament presets in PrusaSlicer or PrusaControl , we already did that for you and the amount of stringing is minimal.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceIf you witness a tiny bit of stringing anyway, you can get rid of it by quickly blasting your finished prints with a heat gun.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceTo achieve the best adhesion of the print surface, it is important to keep it clean.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceUsing of isopropyl alcohol is not recommended, because the adhesion may be too strong.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceYou can use the glue stick as a separator however, a better choice is a window cleaner.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing advicePour a small amount of window cleaner on an unscented paper towel and wipe the print surface.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceThe bed should be cleaned when it’s cold for the best results.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceIf it is cleaned when already preheated for PETG, keep in mind that the cleaner will evaporate before it can clean anything.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceAlternatively, you can clean the bed with warm water and a few drops of dish soap on a paper towel.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceWhen post-processing PETG, it’s possible to use both dry and wet sanding.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceWhen printing with PETG, you must consider using a cooling fan.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceThe rapid cooling helps to keep print detailed with no stringing and blobs.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceIf you need the strongest possible print, print with no fan.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceWe recommend printing the first few layers without the cooling fan to prevent warping and half fan power on after that.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
  • Printing adviceIf you’re in need of a durable part, increase the number of perimeters rather than increasing the infill percentage as the majority of a 3D print strength comes from its outer shell.Prusa Research, Prusament PETGp. 1
